messages.author: 4c16debd333db67f
messages.subject: warning on parboot
parts:
Hello, I'm attempting to bootstrap fitstats using partboot() with 100 replicates of a gmultmix() model (with NB errors) and am getting this error:

 

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :

  3 nodes produced errors; first error: non-finite finite-difference value [16]


The parboot object isn't created so I'm having trouble digging into this to diagnose.

The model I'm trying to bootstrap runs fine on its own, but seems to melt down when run iteratively in the bootstrap..

My general question is... what's going on? and my specific questions are (1) what is a node (is that one of the model iterations?); (2) what does "non-finite finite-difference value" refer to?; and (3) what does the subscripted [16] refer to? (I'm guessing iteration number?)

As an aside, I don't get this error when bootstrapping the same model with Poisson errors, but that model's c-hat is 3.5 and its fit statistics are all very poor so I'd like to compare with the NB model.

Thanks in advance for any insights or help!

Mark

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: warning on parboot
parts:
That error is probably coming from the optimization that runs for each bootstrapped replicate.

Try setting the argument parallel=FALSE in your call to parboot(). Most likely it will still give you an error, but it might be a more informative error. Does it crash immediately or only after a while?

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] warning on parboot
parts:
Here's a wild guess:  the default method passed on to optim from gmultmix is "BFGS" which uses a finite difference method to estimate a gradient (if you don't specify an explicit gradient).  One or more of your bootstrap samples must not work so well using this method.  Maybe adding in method="Nelder-Mead" to the initial gmultmix command would help.

Jim

With method="Nelder-Mead":

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 
  3 nodes produced errors; first error: function cannot be evaluated at initial parameters

With default optimization (BFGG);

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

I'm not sure how to interpret these errors. Do you have any thoughts on what I should try next to get the bootstrap to run? Again, it works okay for the Poisson version of the same model, but that model has c-hat of ~3.5 so I'd like to compare to the model with NB errors.

Thanks for your help. Best wishes,

Mark

Mark,

I'm guessing this error is related to the pre-release version of unmarked you're using - parboot is generating a simulated dataset that the c++ likelihood function is choking on for some reason.
I'll get in touch via email try try to sort it out.

Ken
